name: Hampi Bazaar
description: The bustling temple side beside the working Virupaksha temple, where the old bazaar street, guesthouses and cafes cluster amid the ruins. It is the historic, sacred core of Hampi, busy with pilgrims and travellers exploring the surrounding monuments on foot.
bestFor: History lovers and first-time visitors who want temples and ruins on their doorstep
pros: Steps from major temples and ruins
Plenty of cheap guesthouses and cafes
Easy to explore the site on foot

name: Virupapur Gaddi (Hippie Island)
tagline: Laid-back paddy-field side across the river
description: The relaxed side across the Tungabhadra, reached by coracle or a long road loop, known for rice paddies, rustic riverside cafes and a mellow backpacker mood. It is quieter and greener than the bazaar, favoured by those wanting to unwind for a while.
bestFor: Slow travellers and backpackers craving a calm, unplugged riverside base
cons: Coracle crossing can stop after dark
Very basic facilities and weak WiFi

name: Kamalapur
tagline: Royal enclosure side with quiet lodging
description: The town near the royal enclosure and archaeological museum, on the southern side of the site. It offers slightly more settled accommodation and services away from the bazaar crush, and sits handy for the grand ruins of the former royal centre.
bestFor: Visitors wanting proximity to the royal ruins with calmer, steadier lodging
pros: Close to the royal enclosure and museum
cons: Fewer traveller cafes and social buzz
A little removed from the river scenery

name: Hospet (Hosapete)
description: The nearest proper town, about 30 to 45 minutes away, and the transport gateway with the closest railhead linking Bangalore and Goa. It has more hotels, shops, ATMs and services than Hampi itself, making it a practical base for supplies and onward travel.
bestFor: Those needing better amenities, train links, shops and reliable services
